blogPosts.title: Education that helps children flourish
blogPosts.excerpt: Education at Creation Care Foundation gives children a place to learn, grow in character, and discover how to care for one another.

cover.alt: Children and mentors gathered together outdoors
cover.caption: Children and mentors gathered for a day of learning.

content.text: Education is one of the ways Creation Care Foundation cares for children. We want every child to have a safe place to learn, to be known, and to grow in confidence as well as knowledge.

Learning here is about more than a lesson. Children practice reading, numbers, and communication, and they also learn how to treat one another with respect. Mentors and teachers stay close so that school is a place of encouragement.

content.alt: A large group of children standing together with their mentors
content.caption: Learning happens in community, with mentors and children side by side.

content.text: We believe children flourish when they are protected, taught, and invited to care for their neighbors and for the world God made. That is why education sits alongside mentorship, child protection, and faithful care for creation.
Churches, families, and partners can help by praying, volunteering, and supporting learning resources so more children can keep coming to a place where they are taught and cared for.

blogPosts.title: Care Nursery and Primary School
blogPosts.excerpt: Care Nursery and Primary School gives young children a safe place to learn, build character, and grow into responsible members of their community.

cover.alt: Children seated together during a lesson at Care Nursery and Primary School
cover.caption: A lesson with children gathered in the school room.

content.text: Care Nursery and Primary School is an investment in children and in the communities they will help shape. It gives young children a strong foundation for lifelong learning, personal development, and responsible citizenship.

content.alt: A teacher speaking with children seated in rows of chairs
content.caption: Teachers lead lessons in a simple, shared classroom.

content.text: The school’s approach goes beyond marks on a page. Children are given a safe and nurturing environment where they can develop knowledge, confidence, creativity, character, and practical skills.

content.alt: Children listening during class, with one child raising a hand
content.caption: Children take part, listen, and ask questions.

content.text: Through early childhood and primary education, children build foundations in literacy, numeracy, communication, and critical thinking. They are also encouraged to care for others, for their community, and for the natural environment.

content.alt: Children and adults seated in a circle inside the school room
content.caption: Learning often happens in a circle, with children and adults together.

content.text: Lessons include practical and experiential activities so curiosity and a love of learning can grow. The aim is that each child becomes a responsible and active member of society, grounded in care for people and for God’s creation.

content.alt: Children and adults posing together inside the school
content.caption: Children, families, and partners gathered at the school.

content.text: Partnerships and gifts help strengthen learning resources, support teachers, and keep the classroom open so more children can learn in a safe and enriching place.

blogPosts.title: Mentoring that walks with people
blogPosts.excerpt: Biblical mentorship walks with children, youth, and emerging leaders through Scripture, prayer, character, and everyday guidance.

cover.alt: Adults standing in a circle and holding hands outdoors
cover.caption: Mentors and neighbors stand together in a community circle.

content.text: Biblical mentorship is one of the heartbeats of Creation Care Foundation. We walk alongside children, youth, and emerging leaders through Bible-based mentoring, character development, leadership training, prayer, and practical life guidance.

content.alt: A community circle of adults holding hands outdoors
content.caption: Mentoring begins when people stand together and commit to one another.

content.text: Mentorship is more than passing on skills. It is presence. Mentors pray with young people, open Scripture together, and offer practical help for school, family life, and the responsibilities of growing up.

The work also belongs to the wider community. Neighbors, church members, and partners gather so that children are not left to grow up alone. A circle of care keeps mentorship honest, shared, and close to home.
If you feel called to become a mentor, we would love to hear from you. Together we can help the next generation follow Christ, serve others, and become faithful stewards in their communities.
